title: Grade 8 Integrated Science Scheme of Work: Simple Electrical Circuits (Synthetic Mock Corpus)
subject: Integrated Science

entries.topic: Simple electrical circuits: Circuit components and circuit diagrams
priorKnowledge: Electricity is used in everyday devices
learningOutcomes: Identify the symbols for a cell, battery, switch, lamp, resistor, ammeter and voltmeter
Build a simple series circuit and draw its circuit diagram
Explain why a circuit must be a complete loop for current to flow
keyConcepts: electric current is the flow of charge
learningActivities: Learners build a circuit with a cell, wires, a switch and a lamp and test the switch
Learners draw the circuit using standard symbols and a ruler
Learners test materials to classify them as conductors or insulators
Learners troubleshoot circuits with a hidden fault such as a loose wire or a broken lamp
resources: Lamps (1.5 V), switches, wires, crocodile clips
Materials to test (metal, plastic, wood, graphite)
entries.assessment: Draw a circuit diagram of a cell, switch and lamp in series and explain why the lamp does not light when the switch is open.
entries.teacherNotes: Use only low-voltage cells and never mains electricity. Learners often believe current flows from both ends of the cell and 'clashes' in the lamp, or that a lamp can light with a connection to only one terminal. Insist on a complete loop and straight, neat lines in diagrams.

entries.topic: Simple electrical circuits: Current and voltage in series circuits
learningOutcomes: State that current is the same at every point in a series circuit
Explain that the voltage of the supply is shared between components in a series circuit
Use an ammeter in series and a voltmeter in parallel correctly
keyConcepts: current measured in amperes (A) using an ammeter connected in series
voltage measured in volts (V) using a voltmeter connected across a component
current is the same everywhere in a series circuit
supply voltage is shared across components in series
adding cells in series increases voltage
adding lamps in series makes each lamp dimmer
learningActivities: Learners build series circuits with one, two and three lamps and compare brightness
Learners measure current at several positions in the circuit
Learners measure voltage across each lamp and across the cell
Learners record results in a table and describe patterns
entries.assessment: Two identical lamps are connected in series to a 3.0 V battery. State the voltage across each lamp.
entries.teacherNotes: Learners think current is used up by the first lamp so the second is dimmer; show with ammeter readings that current is the same. Learners often connect ammeters in parallel and damage them, so check connections before switching on. Use identical lamps so that voltage is shared equally.

entries.topic: Simple electrical circuits: Parallel circuits and comparing circuits
learningOutcomes: Describe how current divides and recombines at junctions in a parallel circuit
State that each branch of a parallel circuit has the same voltage as the supply
Compare series and parallel circuits and explain why homes use parallel wiring
keyConcepts: total current is the sum of branch currents
voltage across each branch equals supply voltage
one branch can fail without stopping others
comparison of series and parallel circuits
learningActivities: Learners build a circuit with two lamps in parallel and measure current in each branch and at the cell
Learners unscrew one lamp and observe the other
Learners measure voltage across each lamp
Learners complete a table comparing series and parallel circuits
entries.assessment: Two identical lamps are connected in parallel to a 3.0 V battery and the current from the battery is 0.60 A. State the voltage across each lamp and the current in each branch.
entries.teacherNotes: Learners often think voltage is shared in parallel circuits as in series circuits. Show that each branch has the full supply voltage. Learners also think current is used up in the branch; show that currents add at the junction.
